articles.title: Korea Box Office: ‘The Assassin(s)’ and ‘Tazza 4’ Dominate Chuseok Holiday Weekend Surge
articles.summary: Director Hur Jin-ho’s political crime thriller “The Assassin(s)” powered to the top of the South Korean box office over the weekend of Sep. 25–27, leading a major holiday box office surge across the peak Chuseok festival frame.
body: “ The Odyssey ” took third place in its eighth weekend, adding $3.2 million from 364,763 admissions across 843 screens. The film took 16.6% of the weekend market. Its haul has reached $96.3 million from 11,783,301 total admissions since its Aug. 5 launch.

Last week’s chart-topper in admissions, “ The Intern,” moved to fourth place in its sophomore frame. Directed by Kim Do-young and starring Choi Min-sik and Han So-hee, the Warner Bros. Korea comedy remake generated $1.5 million from 206,347 admissions across 722 screens, capturing 7.6% of receipts. That lifted its cumulative total to $5.3 million from 756,057 viewers.

Auteur Lee Chang-dong’s social drama “Possible Love” debuted in fifth place, earning $557,981 from 72,022 admissions across 195 screens. The Venice Grand Jury Prize winner stars Jeon Do-yeon, Sul Kyung-gu, Cho Yeo-jeong, and Zo In-sung, centering on the psychological tension between a working-class couple in the aftermath of a strike and a wealthy couple filming a documentary about them. Since its Sep. 23 bow, South Korea’s Oscar submission has amassed $890,241 from 115,938 admissions.

articles.title: Kacey Musgraves Pays Heartfelt Tribute to Dolly Parton With ‘I Will Always Love You’ Performance at MTV Video Music Awards
articles.summary: Kacey Musgraves led a touching tribute to Dolly Parton at the MTV Video Music Awards 2026, honoring the late country icon just a month after her death with a rendition of “I Will Always Love You.” The pre-taped performance began with footage of Parton introducing the classic 1974 tune.
body: Following Parton’s death in August, Musgraves dedicated her song “Rainbow” to Parton at her concert at Boston’s TD Garden, followed by a rendition of her 1977 classic “Here You Come Again.” Then, at her “Middle of Nowhere” tour stop at New York City’s Madison Square Garden just a few days later, she covered “9 to 5,” a song that she’d included in her shows over the years.

“I’m not over it, and I’m never gonna be over it,” she told the MSG crowd regarding Parton’s death. “The world definitely lost a light, and it’s hard for me to talk about. And I know how much Dolly meant to everybody also in this room. I think why it feels so dark is it’s already hard to navigate these times right now, and then we lose a matriarch like that. It’s the closest thing we’ve ever had to royalty.”

Musgraves had also shared the stage with Parton at the 2019 MusiCares Person of the Year event, where she kicked off a tribute to the country icon alongside Katy Perry for a duet on “Here You Come Again.” The Queen of Nashville herself then joined them in a white dress with flowing sleeves.

articles.title: Madonna Opens MTV Video Music Awards With Sabrina Carpenter and Charli xcx, Plus Sombr, Debi Mazar and More
articles.summary: Madonna performed for the first time in 23 years at the MTV VMAs on Sunday, opening the show by bringing out special guests Sabrina Carpenter and Charli xcx to perform their respective duets.
body: Madonna has been a perennial fixture at the VMAs since its inception, dating back to her iconic performance of “Like a Virgin” at the show’s 1984 debut. In the decades that followed, she performed “Express Yourself” in 1989, “Vogue” in 1990, “Ray of Light” with Lenny Kravitz in 1998 and, of course, alongside Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera during her last VMAs performance in 2003.
She also led all other artists in nominations for the 2026 VMAs, earning 13 nods. Taylor Swift followed with 11 nominations, Sabrina Carpenter with nine and Ariana Grande with eight.

Days before her appearance, VMAs producer Van Toffler spoke with Variety about bringing Madonna back to the stage. “Well, look, we can deny it as much as we want, but Madonna is the M in MTV,” he said. “I knew it the day I started there. She is the queen of MTV. She makes great videos. She’s provocative. She always pushed us, and this year’s performance will be no exception.”

articles.title: Taylor Swift at the 2026 MTV VMAs: Pop’s Biggest Star Accepts Inaugural Artist Director Honor, Debuts Music Video
articles.summary: The superstar singer-songwriter recently released a special edition of her 'Life of a Showgirl' album, 'The Life of a Showgirl: Encore Edition.'
body: Taylor Swift was awarded the inaugural Artist Director Honor at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards Sunday night.

The Life of a Showgirl singer was introduced by friend Dakota Johnson. “Taylor Swift is a storyteller,” Johnson told the crowd. “She is an architect of emotional landscapes filled with the most intimate and intricate details.”

Swift thanked MTV for giving this platform to music videos “so long ago.” She also thanked her fans. The singer noted she’s been a part of making 60 music videos, 18 of which she wrote and directed herself. She then introduced the music video for her latest single “Patient Zero,” starring Johnson and Colin Farrell.

Hosted by Snoop Dogg, the 2026 MTV VMAs aired on CBS and MTV. The show is taking place live from Los Angeles — well, almost live. The Ravens-Cowboys game on CBS delayed the televised start of the show by roughly 20 minutes; however, the ceremony started in person on time, meaning those in the audience in L.A. are seeing what happens before the viewers at home do.

articles.title: Chuck Lorre Pulls No Punches in Politically Charged Speech Aimed at President Trump, “Far-Left Woke Culture” and Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
articles.summary: The super producer and prolific and generous philanthropist took center stage Saturday at Project Angel Food's Angel Awards. He responded with a punchline-filled speech that included targets like Melania Trump, "a surgically-enhanced, cold-hearted Yugoslavian escort who clearly hates her husband."
body: When Chuck Lorre ‘s daughter, Nikki, fielded a phone call from her famous father to ask if she’d be up for presenting him with a founders award at a Project Angel Food fundraiser, she was “obviously beyond honored and humbled.”

Once he got the Trump dig out, the audience erupted with laughter and Lorre expressed his relief. “OK, I do have the right audience,” he said as he scanned the crowd. “I’d love to express my gratitude to all the people who’ve devoted their lives to making Project Angel Food an oasis for those in need. That would be my preference. But because I’m a comedy writer, I have no choice but to explain how I wake up every morning to turn on CNN to see if the President of the United States had a heart attack while straining to take a dump.”

articles.title: 5 Star Trek: Deep Space Nine Episodes With Great Space Battles
articles.summary: Compared to some other Star Trek shows, Deep Space Nine is overflowing with terrific space battles. Here are five episodes that showcase the best of the best.
body: Yet contrary to what you might expect from the stationary setting, "Deep Space Nine" was the most action-packed and propulsive "Star Trek" show yet. Case in point: The pilot, "Emissary," actually shows the vaunted Battle of Wolf 359, where a Borg cube slices up a 40-ship-strong Federation fleet. On "Star Trek: The Next Generation," only the aftermath of Wolf 359 was shown, but "Deep Space Nine" threw viewers into the trenches; the series' lead, Ben Sisko (Avery Brooks), was on the USS Saratoga during Wolf 359.
Both the original "Star Trek" and "The Next Generation" have some episodes with thrilling space battles, but thanks to the Dominion War, "Deep Space Nine" has them far outranked.

In 49 BC, Julius Caesar defied orders of the Roman Senate and brought his troops over the Rubicon River into Italy. History says that before doing so, Caesar declared, "Alea iacta est" — "The die is cast." Those four translated words have become an idiom meaning someone has done something that can't be undone, but they're remembered as a confident, badass boast because Caesar won. What if he hadn't?

articles.title: 5 Forgotten '60s Sitcoms That Still Hold Up Today
articles.summary: We're taking a time machine back to the 1960s to look at 5 forgotten sitcoms that still hold up today (although some of them are almost impossible to find).
body: The television sitcom has been with us since the 1940s, but the form wasn't perfected until the 1950s with the premiere of "I Love Lucy." Then came "The Honeymooners," "Leave It to Beaver," "Father Knows Best" and the raucously funny "The Phil Silvers Show," which gave us military conman Sgt. Bilko. The half-hour format quickly became a favorite of TV viewers, leading networks to seek out other popular comedy personalities around whom they could build a ratings smash.

The 1960s brought us two of the greatest sitcoms in the history of the medium ("The Dick Van Dyke Show" and "The Andy Griffith Show"), but networks allowed creators to get a little zanier with their concepts. There were fun fantastical shows like "Bewitched" and "I Dream of Jeannie," and downright awful ones like "My Mother, the Car." There was also "Gilligan's Island," which became a syndication juggernaut after lasting only three seasons.

articles.title: Snoop Dogg Pokes Fun at Madonna in VMAs Monologue: “She Ain’t a Virgin No More”
articles.summary: The “Drop It Like It's Hot” rapper hosted the 2026 awards ceremony on Sunday.
body: Snoop Dogg knows how to wow a crowd, and the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards was no exception.

The rapper hosted the ceremony at Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater, where he kicked off the festivities by poking fun at Madonna, who opened the show and took home multiple awards, and shared a special shoutout to his hometown of L.A. The 2026 VMAs is the first time the show has taken place in L.A. since 2017’s ceremony, which was hosted by Katy Perry at The Forum.

“I’m grateful to be in the company of some of my favorite people,” Snoop continued. “Madonna, Taylor Swift, Shaboozey, Lisa, Bruno Mars and my girl, Raye — just to name a few. Now, we got a lot of people in here tonight that’s ready to party. Before we get this show started, I want to make sure that you are ready to have some fun, OK?”

Elsewhere during the show, Snoop introduced Raye, who is nominated for song of the year for her smash single, “Where Is My Husband!” and best visual effects for “Click Clack Symphony.” The “Nuthin’ But a ‘G’ Thang” rapper said that he was one of Raye’s “biggest fans” before the British singer made her VMA debut with a performance of “Husband!”

articles.title: You Didn't Watch One Of The Funniest Shows Ever On Peacock, So Watch It On Netflix Now
articles.summary: This hilarious show was greenlit by Peacock, canceled, and eventually Netflix picked it up for one final season. It may be over, but it's still worth watching.
body: This is a ridiculously good premise, and the show delivers. Peacock ultimately declined to keep it going after season 2 and Netflix picked it up. (I can't prove this, but considering that Tina Fey and Robert Carlock are two of the show's executive producers, I'd wager a guess that their combined star power encouraged Netflix to take a chance here.) So why did the show end after just three seasons... and why should you watch it anyway?

Together, the girls of Girls5Eva decide to launch a comeback, using an abandoned mall as a backdrop for an impromptu performance of "Dream Girlfriends" (a song with lyrics like "We've got the kind of birth control that goes in your arm / And tell me again why Tarantino's a genius?") and enlisting the help of Max Martin-style pop genius Alf Musik (Stephen Colbert) to write another surefire hit before they realize they've aged out of their old style. With new, original songs like "BPE" (Google it, I can't spell it out here), "4 Stars," and "The Medium Time," they forge ahead with their comeback... even if that means playing to an empty Madison Square Garden on Thanksgiving morning.

articles.title: Taylor Swift Debuts Music Video for New Single “Patient Zero” Starring Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell at 2026 VMAs
articles.summary: The singer premiered the music video exclusively at the 2026 onstage after accepting the inaugural artist director honors.
body: Taylor Swift dropped the music video for her latest single “Patient Zero” during the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards Sunday night.

After an incident at an event, Farrell makes a comment to Johnson that he thought “she was different,” which leads the actress to ask who she’s different from. The video cuts to Swift living out exactly what Johnson’s been living through, revealing that Farrell poisoned Swift, leading to her death. The music video ends where it began, Johnson looking at a grave, only it’s now revealed that it’s Swift’s grave. The actress leaves a rose atop the gravestone for the woman.

“Patient Zero” one of four new songs on the singer’s special deluxe edition of her latest album, The Life of a Showgirl: Encore Edition. She released the new version of the album on Friday, which featured the other new songs “Babylon,” “Pink Clouding” and “Cleveland!”
